visual_anchors.morphology_description: Dense multi-whorled rosette of 24 lanceolate (lance-shaped) leaves radiating from a central point at the top of the stem. Leaves are elongated, slightly curved, with pointed tips. Brown ink vein lines visible on several leaves. Two overlapping whorls: an outer whorl of ~12 larger spreading leaves and an inner whorl of ~12 shorter/narrower leaves. No flowers, no buds, no branching.
Single unbranched vertical stem rising from the root collar to the leaf crown. No lateral branches. Stem width is moderate. Brown ink lines over green wash. Approximately 80 normalized units tall.

Single bulbous collar node at the base of the stem where the fibrous roots originate. This is the ONLY nodal structure on the root system — no secondary tubers or discrete bulbs are present. The collar is ovoid/globose.

Fibrous taproot system descending from the collar node. Multiple fine root strands spread downward and outward with visible parallel striations painted in red-brown ink. No tubers or secondary nodules. The overall root form tapers to a narrow point at the bottom.

Small pen-drawn anthropomorphic or zoomorphic figure standing to the lower-right of the root system. The figure appears to have a rounded head (possibly with ears), a torso, and arms. It is drawn in brown ink with no color wash. This is a 'mandrake-type' root figure, consistent with medieval herbal manuscript tradition. No text label is associated with this figure in the transcription.

7 lines of Voynichese text arranged as a dense paragraph in the upper-left quadrant of the folio, above and to the left of the plant illustration. Lines 6 and 7 contain bisection markers indicating the text was physically interrupted by the plant's stem or crown.
Irregular pale blue-grey watercolor wash patch on the left-center portion of the folio. Likely pigment bleed through the page from a facing folio, or a deliberate background wash.
